open_points.subject: owner session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin”
open_points.question: What exact cookie scope and attributes implement “only to Registry's own origin,” given that browser cookies are scoped by host/domain and path rather than by origin or port?
options: Host-only cookie with Path=/, HttpOnly, Secure whenever possible, and a declared SameSite value
Domain-scoped cookie with a restricted path and a declared SameSite value
Rely only on HttpOnly and conditional Secure
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only Path=/ cookie with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict.

open_points.subject: owner request concurrent with sign-out
open_points.text: “a request that passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs” and “A sign-out is applied in turn with the session's other requests”
open_points.question: If a request passes the session check but is waiting for the session lock when sign-out takes the lock first, does that already-admitted request still execute, or is session validity checked again after the lock is acquired?
options: Every request admitted before sign-out completes even if sign-out obtains the lock first
Lock order is decisive; a request behind sign-out is refused
Validity is checked again after acquiring the lock
open_points.default_guess: Make lock order decisive and refuse a request that acquires the lock after sign-out.

open_points.subject: confirmation input binding
open_points.text: “the inputs it is bound to, and the inputs it is bound to, and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order”
open_points.question: What exact canonical representation and digest algorithm bind structured inputs, optional or blank values, collections and their ordering to a confirmation?
options: Hash a canonical State 6 serialization with an explicitly fixed algorithm
Hash normalized domain values in a separately declared field order
Store and compare the bound values directly instead of only their digest
open_points.default_guess: Hash a length-delimited canonical serialization of normalized domain values with SHA-256.

open_points.subject: accepted import and refused confirmations in other sessions
open_points.text: “A refused confirmation keeps it” and “An accepted import drops the uploaded file of every owner session; a confirmation shown in another session is refused because the import is closed”
open_points.question: Does a confirmation refused because another session already accepted the import keep its session's uploaded file, or is that refusal an exception because the successful import already dropped it?
options: The successful import drops it; this refusal is an explicit exception
Every refused confirmation keeps it, so the successful import must not drop that session's file
The confirmation is invalidated and both its file and pending confirmation are cleared
open_points.default_guess: Treat closure refusal as an exception: the file has already been dropped.

open_points.subject: cross-session import concurrency
open_points.text: “The requests of one owner session that change its state ... are applied one at a time” and “An accepted import drops the uploaded file of every owner session”
open_points.question: How are an accepted import and concurrent uploads, mapping displays or confirmations in other owner sessions ordered so that no upload can be stored after the closure check but after the successful import has dropped all files?
options: Serialize every import-related operation across all owner sessions with one import lock
Recheck the closure immediately before storing an upload or mapping result
Allow an already-admitted upload to finish, then immediately discard its file if closure exists
open_points.default_guess: Serialize all import uploads, mapping operations and confirmations on one instance-wide import lock.

open_points.subject: cross-session import cleanup failure
open_points.text: “An accepted import drops the uploaded file of every owner session” and “An accepted import stores ... in one transaction”
open_points.question: Is dropping every session's in-memory file part of the import's success boundary, and what happens if cleanup cannot be completed after the store transaction commits?
options: The store commit defines success and cleanup is mandatory best-effort afterward
Success is not returned until all session files are dropped
The files are invalidated by a generation marker atomically with closure, then reclaimed separately
open_points.default_guess: Atomically invalidate all uploaded files with an import generation marker at closure commit, then reclaim their memory.

open_points.subject: configuration variable set
open_points.text: “The configuration is the set of environment variables whose names begin with REGISTRY_” and “It holds exactly these items and no other”
open_points.question: What are the exact environment-variable names for every listed item?
options: State 2 declares fixed names
A later contract declares fixed names
Names are implementation-defined despite unknown REGISTRY_ variables being refused
open_points.default_guess: Declare one fixed REGISTRY_ name for each listed item in the specification.

open_points.subject: configuration well-formedness
open_points.text: “each well formed” and “A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start”
open_points.question: What makes each location, credential, token and backup key well formed, including the character encoding used to measure a secret's 32-byte minimum and compare secret equality?
options: UTF-8 environment text with explicit path and secret syntax rules
Opaque operating-system bytes where supported
A fixed encoded form such as base64 for every secret
open_points.default_guess: Require canonical absolute paths and base64-encoded secret bytes, measuring and comparing the decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: configuration check precedence
open_points.text: “The checks run in one order and the first that fails stops the start: every item of rule 1 present and none unknown” and “Within one check, items go in the order rule 1 lists them”
open_points.question: When missing and unknown variables coexist, or several unknown REGISTRY_ variables exist, which failure is first, since unknown variables have no position in rule 1's item order?
options: Check missing listed items first, then unknown names in lexical order
Check unknown names first in lexical order, then missing items
Report all presence and unknown-name failures together
open_points.default_guess: Check listed items for presence in their declared order, then unknown names lexically.

open_points.subject: backup encryption
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” and “A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with”
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption format, algorithm, nonce generation, key derivation and key-digest algorithm define an encrypted backup and detect ciphertext or metadata tampering?
options: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope and algorithms
Leave the cryptographic format to each implementation
Use storage-level encryption only
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope with a random nonce and authenticate the clear metadata as associated data.

open_points.subject: backup of a store with no audit entries
open_points.text: “It records ... the last audit sequence number it holds” and “checks ... that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number”
open_points.question: What sequence value is recorded and checked when the store has never written an audit entry?
options: Record zero and require an empty audit log
Record an explicit null value
Omit the sequence field until the first entry
open_points.default_guess: Record 0 and require the audit log to be empty.

open_points.subject: backup filename prefixes across releases
open_points.text: “Kept and temporary names begin with two different prefixes the release declares”
open_points.question: Must these prefixes remain stable across releases, or must a new release recognize every earlier prefix so that old backups are still displayed and deleted after 30 days?
options: Prefixes are permanently stable
Each release recognizes all historical prefixes
A release migration renames all existing backup files
open_points.default_guess: Keep permanent, version-independent prefixes and put format versions after the prefix.

open_points.subject: unreadable kept-backup metadata
open_points.text: “The owner interface shows the instant of the newest kept backup, read from the kept backups” and “every file under the kept prefix whose unencrypted record ... cannot be read” is deleted during a run
open_points.question: Before a backup run deletes it, what does the owner interface do when a kept-prefix file has unreadable metadata: ignore it, refuse the view, or report that backup state is invalid?
options: Ignore unreadable files when selecting the newest backup and show a warning
Refuse the backup-status view
Show no newest backup until the next run removes the file
open_points.default_guess: Ignore it for newest-backup selection and show a non-sensitive warning.

open_points.subject: backup file processing order
open_points.text: “It takes the files in the order of their names”
open_points.question: What comparison defines name order: raw filename bytes, Unicode code points, locale order or filesystem enumeration order?
options: Raw filename-byte lexical order
Unicode code-point order
Filesystem enumeration order

open_points.subject: daily backup guarantee
open_points.text: “the days this rule and rule 5 leave without a kept backup are allowed” and “A tested restore exists every day”
open_points.question: Is a checked backup guaranteed to exist for every day, or are days without any newly kept backup permitted after a missed, overlapping or failed run?
options: Days without a newly kept backup are permitted and the consequence must be qualified
A checked backup is mandatory every day and missed or failed runs require a catch-up
An older kept backup is enough for the phrase ‘exists every day’
open_points.default_guess: Permit days without a new backup and qualify the consequence to successful runs.
